summary: Keep every retired claim and envelope identity in a ledger that only grows

replay.detail: No replay. A background job unions existing checkpoint tombstones into the ledger, 4,096 rows per writer transaction with a committed cursor; it resumes after a restart. Later checkpoint recordings and deletions reach the ledger by trigger.

schema.detail: Adds WITHOUT ROWID tables retired_claim_ids, retired_envelopes, retired_claim_withdrawals and retired_envelope_withdrawals, plus six triggers on checkpoint_claims and checkpoint_envelopes (AFTER INSERT, AFTER UPDATE, BEFORE DELETE). Storage version stays 20; earlier binaries open the store and the triggers keep the ledger current. Synthetic SQLite 3.51 measurement, random insertion order, 4 KiB pages: 41.4 B per retired claim ID and 61.1 B per envelope identity (1,000,000 rows each). The local member held 1,136,087 claim tombstones on 2026-10-18; at those rates its ledger is roughly 47 MB of claim IDs plus about 61 MB per million envelope tombstones. This is an estimate, not a measurement of a production store.

rules.detail: Admission, evidence, checkpoint planning, manifests and digests still read checkpoint_claims and checkpoint_envelopes; nothing reads the ledger yet. Adoption still withdraws tombstones from those tables exactly as before.

compatibility.detail: No wire, client or backup format change. A restore rebuilds the ledger from the restored tombstones through the triggers; withdrawal labels are local and not part of backups.

downtime.detail: Normal restart; the tables and triggers are created empty at open. The import runs after startup on the writer queue, in pages, with a 50 ms pause between pages.

recovery.detail: Swapping back to an earlier binary is supported; the ledger and triggers remain and are harmless. Nothing reads the ledger yet, so no behavior depends on it.
